To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the distribution of the mean response in developmental neurotox experiments is skewed, and that the skewness is not due to the skewness of the individual litter distributions, but to the variation of the mean response from one litter to the next.
a hierarchical model for the skew-normal distribution is developed with application in developmental neurotoxiciology.
the unconditional distribution of the mean from a skew-normal distribution with random location parameter is a skewed distribution with a closed-form expression.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the distribution of the mean response when the location parameter is a random variable and the application of this distribution in developmental neurotoxiciology.
the development of statistical methods for the analysis of developmental neurotoxicological data.
the derivation of the distribution of the mean response in the case of a hierarchical skew-normal distribution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hierarchical model for the mean of a skew-normal distribution is a useful tool in the statistical analysis of data from a developmental neurotoxicological experiment.
the skew-normal distribution is a flexible and powerful tool for the analysis of data in developmental neurotoxiciology.
the skew-normal distribution is a very useful tool for modeling data that exhibit skewness and heavy tails.

a hierarchical model for the skew-normal distribution is proposed.
we derived the distribution of the mean response in developmental neurotoxin experiments where the mean response itself is a random effect.

the distribution of the mean response is skewed even if the underlying response distribution is normal.
